Nina (eng-runtime): quick thread: idea to make autoscaling decisions energy-aware and SLO-weighted instead of raw token pressure. keeps dedicated pool costs predictable and aligns with sustainability goals. thoughts?
Carlos (orch): interesting. do you mean scaler uses a composite metric like weight=slot_usage*SLO_priority*efficiency_score ?
Nina (eng-runtime): yes. SLO_priority from tenant tier, efficiency_score from node-level perf (tokens/sec/W), slot_usage from admission token pressure. scaler uses weight to prioritize which pools to expand first.
Rae (sre): i like the observability angle, but complexity: need consistent measurement for W (watts). we already export GPU power draw but unstable. need smoothing and fallbacks.
Ivy (product): product wants predictable latency tiers. if we use energy to route scale, customers must still get the promised p99. how do we guarantee that?
Carlos (orch): proposal: two-phase decision. first compute desired_headroom by SLO and recent miss-rate. second, choose nodes to add ranked by efficiency_score until headroom satisfied. if efficiency_score low, fall back to fastest nodes.
Nina (eng-runtime): headroom computed from lane configs: desired_pct_headroom = base_headroom + tier_multiplier * recent_spike_index. admission proxy signals spike_index via token-pressure.
Rae (sre): operational hooks: expose efficiency_score_raw, efficiency_score_smoothed, headroom_gap, scale_decision_reason. alert if we pick low-efficiency nodes > 50% of adds in 10m.
Ivy (product): also want a fail-safe: if p99 degrades, immediately prefer latency-first scaling for that tenant until metric recovers. customer-facing SLA not impacted.
Carlos (orch): implement fail-safe as a transient override flag: autoscaler subscribes to a p99-channel; flag forces scale_mode=latency for N minutes. simple and stateless.
Nina (eng-runtime): config surfaces: lane -> {base_headroom, tier_multiplier, hedge_factor, prefer_efficiency: true/false}. defaults: premium prefers latency, standard prefers efficiency.
Rae (sre): metrics to add: node_power_watts, node_tokens_per_watt, tenant_p99_by_lane, headroom_shortfall, efficiency_choice_rate. runbooks: when efficiency_choice_rate high + p99 regressing -> disable efficiency heuristic.
Ivy (product): billing question: if we favor efficiency (cheaper nodes), cost-per-token might change. need to translate that into transparent billing lines so customers see cost vs SLA tradeoff.
Carlos (orch): scaler doesn't change billing contract. it just chooses which physical nodes to allocate. billing line items include node-class and effective unit_price. we'll correlate in reports.
Nina (eng-runtime): admission->autoscaler signal: token_pressure events include tenant_lane and estimated_slots_needed. autoscaler aggregates per-pool. keep everything event-driven to avoid heavy intent APIs.
Rae (sre): safety: if power telemetry drops out, autoscaler must default to latency-first. don't trust stale efficiency. OrchBot: plan to stage feature flag "efficiency-aware-scaling" to test on non-critical pools.
OrchBot: rollout scheduled: efficiency-aware-scaling -> canary at 2026-05-12T08:00:00Z. smoke tests: p99 reaction, efficiency telemetry degradation, node-selection logs.
Ivy (product): i'll draft customer messaging and define acceptable p99 guardrails for canary.
Carlos (orch): i'll prototype ranking function and a small sim that replays token-pressure traces.
Rae (sre): i'll add dashboards and a kill-switch alert.
Nina (eng-runtime): awesome. if canary looks good we can extend heuristics to burst lanes and consider energy credits for green-cost tiers. short RFC incoming.
